question: What primary role does a nurse hold regarding hospital equipment on the ward?
explanation: Nurses are directly responsible for the safe handling, maintenance, and oversight of ward equipment during daily patient care duties. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h1)

question: A sphygmomanometer belongs to which general category of hospital equipment?
explanation: Diagnostic tools are used to assess and measure physiological parameters, which blood pressure cuffs are designed to do. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h1)

question: How should an electrical device be disconnected from a wall socket?

options.A: Yank the flexible cord sharply from a distance
options.B: Twist the cable until the prongs snap loose
options.C: Grip the molded plug firmly and pull straight out
options.D: Switch off the main breaker without touching the plug

explanation: Pulling by the cord strains internal wiring and damages the plug assembly, whereas pulling the molded plug protects the electrical connection. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h2)

question: Why is returning battery-operated equipment to charging stations immediately after use crucial in under-resourced settings?

options.A: It prevents nurses from having to clean the outer casing
options.B: It automatically updates the hospital's central financial inventory
options.C: It guarantees readiness during unpredictable power supply failures
options.D: It prevents the device from accumulating dust on the ward floor

explanation: Unstable electrical grids mean devices must be charged whenever possible to remain operational during sudden outages. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of the initial cleaning step before sterilization?

options.A: Removal of organic debris that shields microbes
options.B: Cooling down heated surgical cutting blades
options.C: Lubricating the internal hinges and screw joints
options.D: Enhancing the shiny metallic appearance of steel

explanation: Blood and bodily fluids protect microorganisms from chemical or thermal agents, making thorough cleaning mandatory before disinfection or sterilization. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h3)

question: Which processing level destroys all forms of microbial life, including bacterial spores?
explanation: Only true sterilization achieves complete eradication of all microbial forms, including highly resistant bacterial endospores. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h3)

question: Where should sensitive medical equipment be kept when not in active use?

options.A: Near open windows exposed to heavy outdoor rainfall
options.B: Stacked tightly in high-traffic nursing station corridors
options.C: Clean, dry, and well-ventilated storage areas off the floor
options.D: Directly on damp tiled floors inside utility store rooms

explanation: Proper environmental conditions protect electronic components and materials from moisture damage and physical contamination. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h4)

question: A nurse discovers a vital infusion pump missing during a shift handover. What is the appropriate initial action?

options.A: Report the missing item immediately through administrative channels
options.B: Ignore the discrepancy until the end of the monthly audit
options.C: Replace the cost of the device personally out of salary
options.D: Blame incoming shift staff for stealing the missing device

explanation: Prompt reporting ensures accountability, helps trace asset movement, and maintains accurate hospital inventory records. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h4)

question: How often should a stethoscope diaphragm be disinfected in a clinical ward setting?

options.A: Once at the start of the morning shift
options.B: At the end of each weekly audit cycle
options.D: Only when visibly stained with blood

explanation: Items making direct contact with multiple patients can transfer pathogens unless decontaminated between each use. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h5)

question: Which of the following practices regarding sharps disposal is unsafe?

options.B: Closing container lids when three-quarters full
options.C: Recapping used injection needles before disposal
options.D: Disposing of needles immediately at the bedside

explanation: Recapping increases accidental needle-stick injury risks and is strongly discouraged by standard safety guidelines. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h5)

question: What is the immediate action a nurse should take upon discovering a defective medical device?

options.A: Hide it inside a bottom drawer to avoid administrative queries
options.B: Remove the item from service and attach a warning tag
options.C: Attempt complex electrical repairs using ward scissors
options.D: Leave it plugged in for the next shift to test

explanation: Immediate removal and clear labeling prevent accidental clinical use of hazardous or malfunctioning equipment. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT an acceptable way to handle a broken infusion pump?

options.A: Sending the tagged device to biomedical engineering
options.B: Attaching a bold warning tag detailing the exact error code
options.C: Documenting the mechanical fault inside the ward logbook
options.D: Leaving it on the medication trolley for someone else to notice

explanation: Leaving broken equipment accessible without warning creates severe clinical hazards for patients and staff. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h6)
